what_it_does: Wafer-scale integration means manufacturing an entire silicon wafer as one giant chip — instead of cutting the wafer into hundreds of small chips and packaging them separately, you wire everything together on the wafer itself, fitting an enormous amount of compute and memory into a very compact space. The vision here is fitting an entire data center's worth of AI processing into one standard equipment rack. The challenge is that designing such a system requires making many interdependent decisions — how big each computing tile should be, how much fast on-chip memory (SRAM) to include, how to stack memory dies on top of compute dies vertically, and how the chips interconnect — and these choices affect each other in complex ways. Titan is an automated design exploration framework that models all these dependencies, prunes physically impossible or unreliable configurations early, and searches the design space efficiently to find configurations that maximize performance within area and cost limits.
